title: Complete every task
prompt: TaskItem is supplied. Write public static List<TaskItem> CompleteAll(List<TaskItem> tasks). Return a new list holding a done copy of every task, in the same order. The list passed in must not change: it keeps the same items, and they are still not done.
hints: A List is a class. If you change the list you were given, who else sees the change?
Create a new list for the result, and add a changed copy of each task to it.
Loop over tasks and Add task with { Done = true } to a new List<TaskItem>. Return the new list.
checks: Practice.CompleteAll(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(1, "Pack", false), new TaskItem(2, "Ship", true) }).SequenceEqual(new List<TaskItem> { new TaskItem(1, "Pack", true), new TaskItem(2, "Ship", true) })
checkLabels: Every task in the result must be done, in the original order.
An empty list must give an empty list.
The list passed in must keep its original, not-done task.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Replaces the items inside the list that was passed in.
Copies the list but never completes the tasks.

feedback: Check two things separately: what the returned list holds, and what the list you were given holds afterwards.
